whole grains (atta, jowar, bajra, ragi) instead of maida and polished rice
steaming, pressure cooking with the water kept, quick stir-frying
raw folate foods daily (sprouts chaat, papaya, salads)

methotrexate, anti-seizure medicines (phenytoin, carbamazepine, valproate, phenobarbital), sulfasalazine, trimethoprim and other antifolate medicines

warnings: Folic acid from tablets and fortified foods has an upper limit of 1,000 mcg per day for adults (ICMR, US and EFSA); food folate has no limit.

High-dose folic acid can hide vitamin B12 deficiency while nerve damage continues; get B12 checked if you have anaemia, tiredness, numbness or tingling, especially if you are vegetarian, vegan, over 50 or take metformin.
Folic acid is found in IFA tablets, prenatal vitamins, B-complex and multivitamins, protein powders and +F fortified rice, atta and maida; add up all products you take.
If you are pregnant or planning a pregnancy, your doctor decides the folic acid dose; doctors usually advise starting before conception.
If you take methotrexate, anti-seizure medicines, sulfasalazine or trimethoprim, ask your doctor before taking or stopping folic acid.
5 mg folic acid tablets and folinic acid (leucovorin) are prescription doses.
General information, not medical advice. Check with a doctor before starting supplements.
